newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli mutual fund redemptions fell in December.
newsitem.headline: Israeli mutual fund redemptions fell in December.

text.p: Israeli mutual fund redemptions fell to 172 million shekels in December, bringing full-year 1996 withdrawals to 4.1 billion shekels, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Monday.

Since the start of November, the Israeli share market has been rallying, which Meitav attributed to progress in Israeli-Palestinian negotiations over Hebron, lower interest rates, passage of the 1997 budget and low share prices.
"All these combined together to create a positive atmosphere around the share market," it said.
In December alone, the Mishtanim index of the top 100 shares rose 6.1 percent, Meitav noted.

Israel's mutual funds have suffered chronic redemptions since the stock market turned sour in 1994. In 1994, net redemptions in the funds reached 11.2 billion shekels, falling to 4.75 billion shekels in 1995, Meitav said.
In 1994-96, it said, the funds suffered redemptions of about 20 billion shekels. That left them with assets of 13.55 billion shekels at the end of 1996, a 15.8 percent decline from the end of 1995.
Redemptions were offset by a nominal 6.5 percent return over the year.
In December, most of the redemptions occurred in funds specialising in bonds. Total fund assets rose 3.4 percent in the month despite the redemptions due to an average weighted return of 3.9 percent.
